analysis: This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and expands the `stop` row of the sampling-parameters table (line 2126). The new text says that Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning spans per request via `ReasoningStopScope`, and tool-call spans when the request parses tool calls. It also says the native block engine matches stop strings over the whole output, and that the reported sequence replays the request's scope. No code, configuration, key handling, wire format, attestation, or cache path changes in the supplied evidence. I checked the surrounding head text (lines 2026-2833), including the MTP, prefix-cache, MiMo, and media descriptions, and they are unchanged context. Against the threat model, the prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected. The `stop` scoping the docs describe is provider-side output post-processing and is not an input to cache identity. The doc states the sampler is not part of prompt or cache identity. It does not touch the encrypted E2E path (A-001, T-008), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), or the fan helper (TB-010). The documented behavior shows no new trust boundary crossing or data exposure. Remaining uncertainty: the doc describes behavior in `ReasoningStopScope` and `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`, which are not in this batch. Whether the code matches the doc, and whether stop matching over reasoning spans leaks reasoning content in any response, is not verifiable from this evidence. No finding is raised, since a doc-only change gives no evidence of a regression.
